input.title: fix(build): preserve calls edges over references on undirected collap…
input.body:
Fixes #2391.

The sort by (source, target, relation) before G.add_edge was added for deterministic collapse order, but that also meant alphabetical order picked the survivor whenever two different relations landed on the same (src, tgt) pair — references always beat calls since "calls" < "references". G.add_edge just overwrites, no merge.

Added a small _RELATION_PRIORITY table so the higher-information relation wins the collapse instead of whichever sorts last. Unlisted relations default to

output.summary: This Pull Request addresses a specific data-loss bug in the graph construction process, ensuring that higher-information relations are preserved over lower-information ones during edge collapses in undirected graphs.
files_summary: graphify/build.py: Updated edge handling to prioritize higher-information relations during undirected graph collapses.
tests/test_build.py: Added tests to validate the fix.
focus_areas: Review the implementation of _RELATION_PRIORITY table and its usage in edge collapse logic.
Ensure that the new test cases cover all relevant scenarios, especially order-dependent behaviors.
potential_risks: The addition of a new priority table might introduce subtle bugs if not thoroughly tested or if it interacts poorly with existing logic.
There is a risk that the fix could unintentionally change behavior in other parts of the codebase, although the author states there should be no regressions.
